subject: Private VPC connectivity — runbook questions, DNS & egress ports
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Adam Liu <adam.liu@fincloud.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC connectivity — runbook questions, DNS & egress ports

Adam — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the handful of items your networking team asked us to confirm so you can close the NetOps checklist. TL;DR: Redwood supports both PrivateLink and VPC peering for Private deployments; we need your allowlist CIDRs + a brief probe window to validate connectivity.

Summary of asks from your side:
- Confirm whether you prefer PrivateLink (AWS interface endpoint) or VPC peering. We recommended PrivateLink for cross-account isolation but both are supported.
- Provide the egress CIDR(s) or specific IP ranges for allowlist. If you plan to use NAT/proxy, share the egress IP(s) and port ranges.
- Confirm if DNS resolution will use your internal resolver (conditional for PrivateLink) and whether split-horizon DNS is in use.
- Open outbound ports: 443 (TLS) required; recommend also allowing 53/UDP for DNS if you run recursive lookups via our managed endpoint probe.
- Let us run a 30-minute probe window (non-production) to validate MTU, TCP MSS, and TLS SNI behavior.

Attached: redwood-privatelink-checklist.pdf (ops checklist) and ingress-egress-cidr-sample.csv (format example).

Next steps / proposed owners:
- You: share final choice (PrivateLink vs peering), egress IPs, and preferred probe window.
- NetOps: confirm DNS behavior and whether a proxy/NAT will terminate TLS.
- Redwood (Marissa): will prepare endpoint details and a short probe script.

If convenient, propose Wed 6/9 10:00–10:30am PT for the probe (we'll limit traffic and only attempt benign TLS handshakes).

Thanks — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Adam Liu <adam.liu@fincloud.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Network Ops <netops@fincloud.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC connectivity — runbook questions, DNS & egress ports

Vivek — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from NetOps: we generally prefer PrivateLink for managed services but need a final cost + maintenance note. For the probe window Wed 10am PT works for us. A couple of specifics from NetOps: 

- Egress: our NAT gateway IPs are currently 34.201.88.14 and 34.201.88.15 (US-West-2). We'll confirm if there will be additional IPs behind the LB.
- Proxy: we do not terminate TLS at our proxy for outbound connections to vendor endpoints; TLS should come from the application hosts.
- DNS: we use split-horizon — internal resolver at 10.10.0.2 for service names, external resolution elsewhere. If PrivateLink is used, we will need instructions for private DNS configuration.

NetOps asked whether your probe needs UDP for DNS (we can open 53/UDP for the window) and whether you will require an inbound connection from Redwood to our VPC (we do not allow inbound unless via PrivateLink).

Adam
Adam Liu
Head of Infrastructure, FinCloud.ai
adam.liu@fincloud.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Adam Liu <adam.liu@fincloud.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC connectivity — runbook questions, DNS & egress ports

Thanks Adam — good details, that helps. Quick technical notes from our ops team: 

- PrivateLink flow: Redwood will create an AWS Network Load Balancer in our account and expose an interface endpoint service name. Your team creates the interface endpoint in FinCloud's VPC and optionally enables private DNS. No inbound VPC peering required.
- Egress/Allowlist: If you will be talking to Redwood-hosted control plane/management APIs (certificate provisioning/metrics), the egress IPs you should allowlist are the two NAT IPs Vivek mentioned. For token/query traffic to model nodes inside the Private deployment, traffic originates from our NLB -> interface endpoint; no additional inbound IPs are needed beyond the endpoint.
- Ports: 443/TCP required. DNS 53/UDP only necessary if you want Redwood's probe to resolve service names via your internal resolver; otherwise we'll use our configured resolver.
- MTU: if you have firewall/inspection, ensure TCP MSS clamping is enabled (we've seen fragmentation with an MTU < 1400).

Attached: privatelink-probe-script.sh (small script we run during the probe) — it's just TLS handshakes and basic HTTP/2 negotiation. We'll not transmit any customer data.

Action items for NetOps (FinCloud):
1) Confirm PrivateLink vs peering decision — if PrivateLink, create interface endpoint in the VPC and share the endpoint ID when ready.
2) Share final egress IP list (confirm if NAT LB will add extra addresses), and open 443 outbound to Redwood's endpoint during probe window. Optional: open 53/UDP during the probe.
3) Provide a preferred 30-min probe start time (Vivek suggested Wed 10:00 PT).

We'll standby for the endpoint creation and will run the probe from our maintenance account. If you want a canary header/cookie to identify probe traffic we can include it.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Network Ops <netops@fincloud.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Adam Liu <adam.liu@fincloud.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC connectivity — runbook questions, DNS & egress ports

Marissa / Vivek — NetOps confirms: 
- We'll proceed with PrivateLink. Endpoint creation scheduled for Wed 6/9 09:30 PT (creating com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-0a1b2c3d). We'll enable private DNS for the service.
- NAT egress IPs confirmed: 34.201.88.14, 34.201.88.15 (no additional IPs expected).
- We'll open outbound 443/TCP to Redwood's endpoint and allow 53/UDP for the 30-minute probe window.
- Please send the probe script and a short IP/host we should monitor on our side (TLS SNI value).

Thanks — NetOps
Network Operations (FinCloud.ai)
